transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling Cymbal Telecom. My name is Sarah. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Hi Sarah. I'm having a really frustrating issue with my cell service. My calls keep dropping.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Oh, I'm very sorry to hear that. Dropped calls are definitely frustrating, but I can certainly look into this for you. To get started, could I please have your full name?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: It's David Lewis.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, David. And for security purposes, to access your account, could you please provide your Cymbal Telecom Customer ID number?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Sure, it's uh... CUST-1028.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Got it. And one last verification step: could you please provide the 4-digit security PIN on the account?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, it's 6395.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect, thank you. I've successfully verified the account. I see you have the Unlimited 5G Mobile Plan. Now, you said you're experiencing dropped calls. Can you tell me a little more about that?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yeah, it's almost always when I'm at home. And specifically, it's when I'm in my basement, which is where my home office is. I'll be on a work call and poof, it just disconnects.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I see, that sounds incredibly disruptive, especially for work. Is this happening with every call you make or receive in the basement?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Pretty much, yes. If the call goes on for more than a few minutes, it's almost guaranteed to drop.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay. And outside of the basement, say on the main floor or outside your house, is the service fine?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, it's perfect. No issues at all. It's just my office.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a very helpful detail. Could you provide me with your full service address so I can check the network coverage map for your specific location?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Sure, it's 452 Oak Street, Pleasantville.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. Please give me about 30 seconds while I pull up the detailed signal map and diagnostics for that address. Do you mind holding for a moment?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: No, that's fine.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for your patience, Mr. Lewis. I've got the map here.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, what does it say?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So, the outdoor 5G signal from our nearest tower is rated as 'Excellent' for your address. However, what you're experiencing is very common and it's called signal attenuation.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Signal attenuation? What's that?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It means the signal strength gets weaker as it passes through physical objects. Things like concrete foundations, metal pipes, and even thick insulation in walls can block or weaken the cellular signal significantly.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So because my office is in the basement, the signal just can't get down there properly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly. The signal has to travel through the ground and then your home's foundation to reach your phone, and by that time, it's too weak to maintain a stable call.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So what can I do? I can't move my office.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Well, we have a perfect solution for this exact scenario. It's a feature called Wi-Fi Calling. Are you familiar with it?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: I think I've seen the term, but I'm not really sure what it does.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It allows your phone to make and receive calls and text messages using your home's Wi-Fi network instead of the cellular network. As long as you have a stable Wi-Fi connection, your call quality will be crystal clear.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Oh, my Wi-Fi is great in the basement. I have a mesh router system. So I could use that for calls?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Precisely. Your phone would seamlessly use the strong Wi-Fi signal in your office for calls, completely bypassing the weak cellular signal issue.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: That sounds fantastic. Does it cost extra?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Not at all. Wi-Fi Calling is a standard feature included for free with your Cymbal Telecom plan.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, that's a relief. So how do I set it up?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can walk you through it right now on your phone. It only takes a minute. First, what type of phone do you have?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: I have an iPhone 14.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great. Do you have the phone with you now?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, I'm talking on it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, perfect. We can do this while we're on the call. First, I need you to go to your phone's 'Settings' app. It's the icon that looks like gears.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, I'm in Settings.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Excellent. Now, scroll down a bit and tap on the 'Phone' option. It has a green icon with a white phone on it.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Alright, tapped on Phone.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: In that menu, you should see an option that says 'Wi-Fi Calling'. Do you see it?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, I see it. It says 'Off' next to it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect. Please tap on 'Wi-Fi Calling'.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now you should see a toggle switch that says 'Wi-Fi Calling on This iPhone'. Please tap that switch to turn it on.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Done. A pop-up just appeared... something about Emergency Calls and 911.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, that's a very important step. It's asking you to confirm your primary address for 911 services. Since you'll be using the internet, it needs your physical location for emergency responders. Please make sure the address shown is correct and then tap to confirm or update it.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, yes, the address is correct. I'm hitting 'Enable'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Excellent. It might take just a few seconds to activate.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, the screen is back to the Wi-Fi Calling menu and the toggle is green now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Fantastic. Now for the final confirmation. Look at the very top left corner of your iPhone's screen, in the status bar. Where it normally just says 'Cymbal', what does it say now?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Let me see... Wow. It says 'Cymbal Wi-Fi'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's the magic signal! That confirms you are now officially using Wi-Fi Calling. From now on, whenever you are connected to your Wi-Fi network, your phone will automatically use it for calls.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So when I go into my basement office, as long as I'm on my Wi-Fi, the calls won't drop?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's correct. Your calls should be as clear and reliable as your internet connection. When you leave the house and disconnect from Wi-Fi, it will seamlessly switch back to the Cymbal cellular network without you having to do a thing.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: This is a game-changer. I can't believe it was that simple. I've been struggling with this for months.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm so glad we could get this resolved for you. It's a powerful feature that's often overlooked. It's designed for exactly these kinds of situations.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Thank you so much, Sarah. This is a huge weight off my shoulders.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You are most welcome, Mr. Lewis. I'm happy I could help. Was there anything else I could assist you with today? Any other questions about your account or our services?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: No, that was my only issue, and you've fixed it perfectly. I'm all set.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Wonderful to hear. Well, thank you for being a Cymbal Telecom customer. We appreciate your business. Have a fantastic rest of your day!

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: You too. Thanks again! Bye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.
